objects.original: One real Hilbert space E, one probability measure μ, one fixed positive real C, actual scalar tests and their E-valued gradients, and scalar/vector L² classes (u,H).
objects.reconstructed: The same E, μ, C, compact smooth scalar tests and genuine gradients, and the same scalar/vector L² classes (f,w).
objects.evidence: The actual declaration uses μ in both Lp factors and every integral. The single witness g defines both a.e. equalities r.1 =ᵐ[μ] g and r.2 =ᵐ[μ] gradient g; these are not independently chosen representative functions. Smoothness makes the gradient the genuine Riesz representative of the derivative.

domains.original: Finite-dimensional complete real Hilbert/Borel E; compact smooth scalar tests for LSI and the starting pairs; joint product-L² norm closure for the conclusion.
domains.reconstructed: A complete finite-dimensional real inner product space with its Borel structure; smooth compact support for the tests and representatives; joint norm closure in L²(μ;ℝ) × L²(μ;E).
domains.evidence: The Lean typeclasses specify this Hilbert/Borel structure; an orthonormal coordinate identification gives the Euclidean setting used in §2.1.1. The actual closure has the product topology of the two normed Lp spaces, not the projection onto the scalar factor, a weak topology, a set of all L² functions, or an abstract reversible-form domain.

quantifiers.original: Fix E, μ and C>0; assume the LSI for every compact smooth v; for every pair in the closure of pairs admitting one common smooth compact witness, conclude PI.
quantifiers.reconstructed: The same universal compact-test premise, one existential common witness per initial pair, and a universal conclusion over the joint closure for fixed μ and C.
quantifiers.evidence: hLSI universally quantifies v independently of p, and hp constrains each p after μ and C are fixed. ∃ g occurs only inside the set being closed, so no pointwise smooth representative for an arbitrary limit pair is assumed or concluded. The mean-zero condition in the printed hint is local to the density perturbation, not a binder on p or on the compact tests.

assumptions.original: Borel probability, C>0, homogeneous function LSI with coefficient 2C on all smooth compact real tests, and joint closure membership for the chosen pair.
assumptions.reconstructed: The same assumptions, expanding homogeneous entropy as ∫v² log(v²) − (∫v²) log(∫v²).
assumptions.evidence: PDF page 30, Example 1.2.27, gives the homogeneous entropy convention; PDF page 60 gives the compact-test scope and factor 2. The actual Lean integral formula uses Real.log; the product at zero is zero, as for the continuous extension t log t. The compact smooth integrands are integrable under a probability law, including the energy and entropy terms. Neither closability, absolute continuity, curvature, a tail moment, nor any supplied PI/approximation estimate is a public premise of this theorem.

conclusion.original: Varμ(u) ≤ C‖H‖²_{L²(μ;E)} for each joint limit pair (u,H).
conclusion.reconstructed: Varμ(f) ≤ C‖w‖²_{L²(μ;E)} for each such pair (f,w).
conclusion.evidence: The actual conclusion is ProbabilityTheory.variance (p.1 : E → ℝ) μ ≤ C * ‖p.2‖^2. The local var identity applies to the L² coercion using Lp.memLp; norm_sq identifies the vector norm squared with the actual integrated energy. These are the genuine variance and squared L² norm on the respective a.e. classes.

scopes.original: An original ASTIS Euclidean closure bridge for the density step left implicit in Chewi; a pairwise bound, not an assertion of a single-valued gradient for arbitrary μ.
scopes.reconstructed: A statement about all pairs in a specified joint norm closure, without asserting that the second component is determined by the first.
scopes.evidence: Printed pp. 48–49/PDF pp. 60–61 give compact Langevin formulas, note more general reversible-process notation, and leave the extension to a wider class to density. Exercise 1.7 (printed 43/PDF 55) requests linearization and gives the centered compact KL hint; it does not state this closure theorem. The reconstruction omits an explanatory nonclaim but logically adds no uniqueness. For μ=δ₀ on ℝ a compact smooth test with value 0 and derivative 1 at 0 yields (0,1) alongside (0,0) in the original pair set; the pairwise bound is still meaningful. The Gibbs consumer obtains closability separately and does not extend this to arbitrary measures or identify an abstract Dirichlet-form or generator domain.

constant_dependencies.original: The same fixed positive C appears in PI as appears in the compact LSI coefficient 2C.
constant_dependencies.reconstructed: The same C appears unchanged; no dependence on dimension, a cutoff scale, or an approximation quality parameter is added.
constant_dependencies.evidence: The compact parent passes the entropy limit Var/2 against 2C times the energy limit ∫‖∇g‖²/4. hcompact imports precisely the resulting C coefficient; hS and closure_minimal preserve it. PDF page 61 states the fixed-constant LSI(C) ⇒ PI(C). This declaration does not define or compare optimal constants on abstract form domains.

review_evidence: Independent comparison of the anti-anchored packet, pinned primary edition, actual Lean signatures and proofs, and packet-bound reader lesson. The verdict is equivalence to the explicitly ASTIS-authored statement, not to a verbatim or independently printed Chewi theorem. Chewi supplies the compact Euclidean LSI and PI normalizations, Exercise 1.7's centered KL linearization, and the reference to a density extension; the joint pair domain is the original, bounded bridge. The compact PI parent centers each actual g without falsely assuming the centered perturbation is compact, produces bounded positive square-root perturbations with all analytic inputs, invokes the genuine compact-test cutoff extension, and passes the two scaled limits. In the new proof, pairing with [1] makes the mean continuous, and variance = ‖u‖²₂ − ⟨[1],u⟩² and vector norm squared are continuous in the respective factors. The two a.e. equalities transport the compact PI bound to the starting set, and closure_minimal passes the closed inequality without assuming density into a larger identified domain. The Gibbs test obtains normalization and closability from the actual potential/weight, produces membership using the actual C¹-domain theorem with both L² inputs, identifies the two graph sets, and rewrites variance and energy back to actual f and ∇f. The proof lesson's first three steps match this proof; its application step has the nonblocking exposition gap below. The hash-verified focused compiler receipt is separate proof/build evidence, not a basis for the semantic verdict. No previous reviewer verdict, audit, or repair was consulted.

exposition_findings.finding: The application text says the existing C¹-domain theorem places the given function and gradient in the graph closure and says no extra moment or domain certificate is supplied, without spelling out that this C¹ f and its genuine gradient must both be in L²(μ). The test and the invoked domain theorem do require these two inputs. They are not the same as an assumed graph-membership certificate or a tail-moment hypothesis on the law.
exposition_findings.recommended_clarification: For a C¹ f with f∈L²(μ) and ∇f∈L²(μ), the existing C¹-domain theorem proves that the two classes are in this very graph closure. Compact LSI remains a premise; no curvature, extra tail-moment assumption on μ, or assumed graph-membership certificate is used.
